Electric distribution has no federal prescriptive inspection interval, so 1.3.3 carries gas intervals with citations and names state rule as the electric route rather than implying a national one.
ISO 14224 was checked for a maintenance priority or urgency taxonomy and none was found. EN 13306 Annex E criticality matrix is used instead.

processes.name: Capture inspection or survey finding
processes.intent: Turn a finding recorded during inspection, survey or patrol into follow-on work.
activities: Record the finding against the originating inspection
Grade or classify the finding under the applicable scheme
Determine whether the finding is remediated on this visit or returned to
Raise linked follow-on work carrying the finding and its grade
Update asset condition

trigger.text: Inspection, survey or patrol result carrying a defect or exception.

inputs.what: Inspection or survey result with condition or grade

outputs.what: Follow-on work linked to the finding

controls.text: A finding can shorten the next interval for the same asset. Atmospheric corrosion found on a service line moves the next inspection from 63 to 39 months, so the due-date calculation must read the outcome of the prior inspection and not only its date.
Where a leak is graded 2, it is reevaluated at least every six months until cleared, and regrading is a full reassessment against the original criteria, not a decrement.
The link from finding to follow-on work is the evidence chain. An unlinked follow-on cannot be shown to close the finding.

controls.text: Federal gas intervals are expressed as a nominal period and a not-to-exceed month figure together - annual and 15 months, three years and 39 months, five years and 63 months. Both bind; satisfying one is not compliance.

Intervals are ceilings that a regulator may lower for a particular operator. A model that treats them as immutable constants will be wrong for operators holding an approved deviation.

processes.name: Apply compliance and due-date rules
processes.intent: Apply the interval that fixes when mandated work must be complete.
activities: Identify the obligation and the population attribute that selects the interval
Read the date and the outcome of the last compliant completion

Record the interval basis for audit

trigger.text: Work carrying a compliance obligation needs a due date.

inputs.what: Date and outcome of last compliant completion

controls.text: Federal gas intervals bind twice - a nominal period in calendar years and a not-to-exceed figure in months. Satisfying the calendar year alone is not compliance.

Some intervals are conditional on the prior outcome, not only the prior date, and some are conditional on asset attributes such as cathodic protection status. A table keyed only on geography will produce wrong due dates.

For electric distribution there is no federal prescriptive interval layer at all. Where an interval is needed it comes from state rule, and the reference names the state exemplar rather than implying a national one.
